subject: Money
title: Central Bank Dilemma
description: A quick, practical guide to Central Bank Dilemma.

hook.text: Alan Greenspan saw the dot-com bubble forming in 1996. He called it 'irrational exuberance.' Then he did nothing.

buildup.text: Central banks face a dilemma: should they pop bubbles early or clean up after the crash?

discovery.text: Popping bubbles means raising rates, which hurts the whole economy. The cure might be worse than the disease.

twist.text: Greenspan chose to clean up after. He cut rates post-crash, which fueled the next bubble in housing.

climax.text: There's no good answer. Act early and you're the villain who killed growth. Act late and you failed to prevent disaster.

punchline.text: Pop it early or pick up the pieces. Both hurt.

quiz.question: What did Greenspan do after identifying 'irrational exuberance'?
options: Did nothing and planned to clean up after
